meta.titre: Malnutrition and Dietary Disorders: Kwashiorkor, Marasmus, Obesity and Eating Disorders
meta.sous_theme: Protein energy malnutrition, obesity and eating disorders

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Imagine a young child at a health centre with swollen feet and a puffy face. At home he eats mostly cassava paste and maize pap because protein foods such as beans, eggs and fish cost too much. At the other extreme, some people in towns eat too many fried and sugary foods and gain too much weight. Both situations are forms of malnutrition. The GCE asks you to name the diseases, tell them apart, and say how each is prevented, usually in a fixed number of points.

items: The body needs a balanced diet containing all the nutrients in the right amounts.
Proteins are needed for growth and repair, and carbohydrates and fats give energy.
Weaning is the stage when a baby begins to eat solid foods in addition to breast milk.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What malnutrition means
Malnutrition is poor nutrition over a long time. The diet has too little of some nutrients (undernutrition), too much (overnutrition), or the wrong balance. An inadequate supply of protein and energy foods leads to protein energy malnutrition (PEM), which has two main forms.

### Kwashiorkor and marasmus
| Feature | Kwashiorkor | Marasmus |
|---|---|---|
| Main lack | Protein, while some starchy food is eaten | Food in general, especially energy foods |
| Usual victim | Young child, often after weaning | Baby or very young child |
| Body shape | Swollen feet, legs, face and belly (oedema) | Very thin, wasted muscles, wrinkled loose skin, no oedema |
| Other signs | Thin, pale or discoloured hair, skin sores, sadness, poor appetite | Weak, irritable, old looking face, constantly hungry |

### Disorders of eating and of excess
- **Obesity** is being very overweight. The cause is eating more energy food than the body uses, with little exercise. It raises the risk of heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes and joint pain.
- **Anorexia nervosa** is an eating disorder in which a person refuses to eat enough because of a fear of becoming fat. The person becomes dangerously thin and weak.
- **Bulimia nervosa** is an eating disorder in which a person eats a large amount and then makes himself vomit or uses other ways to get rid of the food.
- **Anaemia** (lack of iron) and other deficiency diseases are also forms of malnutrition.

### Prevention
Breast feed the baby; introduce protein foods such as beans, groundnuts, eggs, fish and soya at weaning; eat a balanced diet in the right amounts; take regular exercise; give health education to families; take the child to a health centre early. Severe malnutrition and eating disorders need medical care.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to differentiate between two diseases or foods.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the difference side by side, one feature at a time, and name both items in each sentence. For two marks write one clear contrast such as: "Kwashiorkor shows swollen (oedematous) limbs and face, but a child with marasmus is wasted and has no oedema." Do not describe only one disease.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for causes, effects or preventive measures with a number.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Count your points. Causes: poverty, ignorance about food, early weaning on starchy pap, famine, illness. Prevention: breast feeding, balanced and varied meals, protein weaning foods, growing food at home, health education, regular weighing of children at the clinic. Write the exact number asked, each with a short reason.

sections.enonce_markdown: A mother says that her 18 month old son has lost his appetite, has swollen feet and sores on the skin, and has been fed mostly on yam porridge since he stopped breast feeding. (a) Name the disease the child is suffering from. (b) Give two reasons for your answer. (c) State two foods that should be added to his diet. (5 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Name", "give two reasons" and "state two foods" are short-answer commands, so each part gets one or two marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part (a) 1 mark, part (b) 2 marks, part (c) 2 marks.

etapes.action: Pick out the clues in the description.
etapes.justification: Swollen feet (oedema), skin sores and loss of appetite appear in kwashiorkor, and a diet of a starchy food after weaning lacks protein.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Clues: oedema, skin sores, poor appetite, starchy diet after weaning.

etapes.justification: A child who is swollen rather than wasted has kwashiorkor, a form of protein energy malnutrition.

etapes.action: Write the reasons as complete statements.
etapes.justification: Each reason must link a sign to the disease.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. The child has swollen feet, which is oedema, a sign of kwashiorkor. 2. His diet of yam porridge is starchy and very low in protein.

etapes.action: Choose protein foods that a family can afford.
etapes.justification: The cure for protein lack is a diet with body building foods.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Beans and eggs (fish, groundnuts or soya would also be accepted).

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Kwashiorkor. (b) Swollen feet (oedema) and a starchy, low protein diet after weaning. (c) Beans and eggs. The child should also be taken to a health centre.

items.erreur_markdown: "Kwashiorkor and marasmus are both caused by lack of vitamins."
items.pourquoi_faux: Both are forms of protein energy malnutrition. Vitamin lack causes other diseases, such as rickets or night blindness.
items.correction_markdown: Say that kwashiorkor is mainly a lack of protein, and marasmus is a lack of food in general, especially energy foods.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that a child with marasmus has a swollen belly and puffy feet.
items.pourquoi_faux: Oedema is the sign of kwashiorkor. A child with marasmus is wasted and very thin.
items.correction_markdown: Marasmus: very thin, wasted, no oedema. Kwashiorkor: swollen feet and face.

items.erreur_markdown: Calling anorexia nervosa a disease caused by eating too much.
items.pourquoi_faux: It is the opposite: the person eats too little because of a fear of becoming fat.
items.correction_markdown: Anorexia nervosa: refusal to eat enough. Bulimia nervosa: eating a large amount and then getting rid of it. Obesity: eating more energy food than the body uses.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing only two preventive measures when the question asks for four.
items.pourquoi_faux: In the Paper 2 mark scheme each correct point earns a mark, so missing points lose marks.
items.correction_markdown: Count your points and give the exact number asked, each with a few words of explanation.

items.enonce_markdown: Name (a) the disease caused by a severe lack of protein in a child, (b) one sign that is seen in that disease but not in marasmus, (c) an eating disorder in which a person vomits after eating a large meal, and (d) one health risk of obesity.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Kwashiorkor**. (b) **Oedema (swollen feet, legs or face)**. (c) **Bulimia nervosa**. (d) Any one of heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes or joint pain, for example **high blood pressure**.

items.enonce_markdown: A health worker advises a mother to prepare a protein weaning meal made from 250 g of beans at $800$ FCFA per kilogram, 2 eggs at $100$ FCFA each and 100 g of groundnut paste at $1\,200$ FCFA per kilogram (assumed prices). (a) Find the cost of one meal. (b) Find the cost of 6 such meals. (c) The mother has $4\,000$ FCFA for the week. How much is left after 6 meals?

A girl of 16 eats very little because she is afraid of becoming fat. She is very thin, tired and often dizzy. Her sister of 20 eats large amounts of fried food and sweets, takes no exercise and is much overweight. (a) Name the disorder of the younger girl. (b) State two harmful effects of her habit on the body. (c) State two health problems the older sister may develop. (d) Suggest three pieces of advice that would help the older sister.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Anorexia nervosa**. (b) Any two of: she becomes dangerously thin; she is weak and tired; she lacks nutrients, which can lead to deficiency diseases such as anaemia; her growth and health suffer. (c) Any two of: obesity-related heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, joint pain. (d) Any three of: eat smaller portions; cut down on fried and sugary foods; eat more vegetables, fruits and fibre foods; take regular exercise such as walking; drink water instead of sweet drinks; see a health worker for guidance.

items_markdown: Malnutrition means poor nutrition caused by too little, too much or the wrong balance of nutrients.
Kwashiorkor is mainly a lack of protein and shows oedema; marasmus is a lack of food in general, especially energy foods, and shows wasting without oedema.
Obesity comes from eating more energy food than the body uses; its risks include heart disease, high blood pressure and diabetes.
Anorexia nervosa is refusing to eat enough from a fear of getting fat; bulimia nervosa is eating a large amount and then getting rid of it.
Prevention: breast feeding, protein weaning foods, a balanced diet, exercise, health education and early medical care.
In Paper 2 give the exact number of points asked, and for "differentiate" write both sides of the difference.
